Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate marked dilation of the trachea and main bronchi (indicated by arrowheads), which is the hallmark radiological feature of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). This distinguishes it from COPD, normal aging, or other conditions listed which do not typically present with such massive central airway enlargement.
